analysis:
The changed files are CI test scripts (.github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py, .github/scripts/test-threat-diagnostics.py) for the PR-review scanner. No provider, coordinator, crypto, attestation, cache or fan-helper code is touched, so the provider-side assets and threats (A-001..A-017, TB-002/003/007/009/010/011, T-041 and the others) are not affected. These are test-only changes with no runtime attack surface, and I found no security regression.

Behavior examined in the tests:
- test-threat-budget.py: the cross-file uncertainty test now expects a handoff to a human with no redundant local rescan, so there is no extra OPUS call.
- A manual GitHub rerun (run attempt 2) must do no paid work and must not clear the merge. The test checks MANUAL_SCAN_RERUN_DISABLED and that clean() is false.
- The scanner runtime is bounded (default 900s, max 3000s). Invalid values are rejected.
- The Bedrock workload ceiling hands off at the exact unadmitted stage and never clears.
- The remaining Bedrock, fallback and diagnostics tests are the existing fail-closed cases: accounting failures, truncation, final uncertainty, call cap, and no leakage of private text into diagnostics.
- test-threat-diagnostics.py: the multi-tier integration test now asserts that plan_calls is invoked with [2, 1], which exercises the new workload planning in budget_scan's integrate().

The tests assert fail-closed behavior (no clearance on error, uncertainty, limit or rerun), which is consistent with the review pipeline's trust model.

Limits on this review:
- The scanner implementation files (threat_review/budget_scan.py, budget_runner, bedrock, merge_policy and others) were not supplied, so I cannot confirm that the production code behind these new test expectations (rerun disabling, workload-call planning, removal of the local rescan) actually enforces them.
- Nothing here shows a weakened control. The removal of the local OPUS rescan after cross-file uncertainty still ends in manual_review_reasons and clean()==False, per the test.
